title: Basic 12 · Loops and stacks
summary: DO loop with a stack.collect child — build a stack from N variations of one operation (e.g. rotations at increasing angles).

steps.title: Try loops and stacks
steps.body: A DO loop (`flow.do`) emits an iteration counter `i`. Wire `i` into Rotate's angle and feed each iteration's output into `stack.collect`, and you get a stack (multi-frame image) built automatically. In cryo-EM nearly everything operates on stacks, so this is a foundational pattern.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Siemens Star**. We'll reuse this one image and build a rotated-variant stack with the loop.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.siemens` shows its image before we build the loop.

steps.title: Drop the DO loop
steps.body: From Control, drag **DO loop** onto the canvas. It's a container-shaped node — whatever you place inside it gets executed start..end times per iteration.

steps.title: Drop Rotate inside DO
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Rotate** and drop it **inside the DO container frame**. Nodes inside a DO run once per loop iteration.

steps.title: Drop Stack collect inside DO
steps.body: From Stack, drag **Stack collect** and drop it **inside the DO container** too. This is the "box that collects every iteration's image" into a stack.

steps.title: Wire Siemens → Rotate.image
steps.body: Drag from the Siemens Star outside the DO to Rotate's `image` input inside. Wires that cross the container boundary are re-read every iteration (the same input image here, every pass).

steps.title: Wire flow.do.i → Rotate.angle_deg
steps.body: Drag from the DO's `i` output (the iteration counter) onto Rotate's **`angle_deg`** param handle (the ◇ to the left of the param). Each iteration will update `angle_deg` with the current `i`, so the rotation angle changes each pass.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. Rotate now runs per iteration with the current `i` as the angle — a baseline before we attach Stack collect.

steps.title: Wire Rotate → Stack collect
steps.body: Drag from Rotate's `image` output to Stack collect's `image` input. Each iteration's rotated image accumulates into the stack.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With the default iteration count, Stack collect already has a few frames — a baseline before we choose a full angular sweep.

steps.title: Click the DO loop
steps.body: Click the DO container header (top bar) to select it. The Inspector reveals `start` / `end` / `step`.

steps.title: Set end to 360
steps.body: Change `end` to **360** — the iteration will stop at 360°.

steps.title: Set step to 90
steps.body: Change `step` to **90**. With start=1 this gives i = 1, 91, 181, 271 — four iterations at roughly 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The DO loop iterates four times; Stack collect accumulates four rotated Siemens Stars. The node preview shows the middle slice (= middle stack frame); the Inspector shows every frame.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Vary the iteration count by changing `end` / `step`, wire `i` into a different param, swap Rotate for Shift or Filter — endlessly extensible. In production cryo-EM you'll often "loop ap_sh / ap_mr over a stack", so the loop + stack.collect pattern is a daily tool.
